headline_summary: Dell Technologies is the integrated US technology hardware franchise, founded 1984 by Michael Dell (still Chairman/CEO 42 years later), now operating at $113.5B FY26 revenue with $24.6B FY26 AI server revenue (+300%+ YoY), $64B AI server orders closed during the year, $25B+ AI server shipped, and a record $43B AI server backlog entering FY27. Q4 FY26 ISG revenue $18.82B (+66% YoY); CSG revenue $13.5B (+14%). Yvonne McGill stepped down as CFO September 9 2025; David Kennedy is interim CFO. Board has unanimously recommended redomestication to Texas.
ipo_history: NASDAQ June 1988; take-private October 2013 ($24.4B LBO with Silver Lake); relisted NYSE December 2018 (DELL ticker)
ceo_chairman: Michael S. Dell (founder; CEO 1984-2004, 2007-present; Chairman since 1984)
coo_vice_chairman: Jeff Clarke (Vice Chairman and COO since December 2019)
interim_cfo_sept_2025: David Kennedy (27-year Dell veteran; prior CSG CFO and Global Sales COO)
key_supplier_nvidia: Dominant AI accelerator GPU supplier; Dell AI Factory Nvidia-optimised
key_supplier_amd: Alternative accelerator GPU (MI300/MI400) plus EPYC CPU
structural_thesis_in_one_paragraph: Dell Technologies is the largest US enterprise IT hardware franchise and one of the most consequential beneficiaries of the AI server demand cycle. The investment proposition is whether the $43B AI backlog converts to revenue at margins that hold against hyperscaler self-sourcing through ODMs (Inventec/Quanta/Wiwynn) and against competitive pressure from Supermicro and HPE, while CSG AI PC refresh provides the second growth engine and the CSG cash-generative base funds the working capital intensity of AI server scaling. The board (Michael Dell + Egon Durban Silver Lake + Ellen Kullman Lead Independent ex-DuPont CEO + William Green Audit Chair ex-Accenture Chairman + Steven Mollenkopf ex-Qualcomm CEO + David Dorman Centerview ex-AT&T + David Grain + Lynn Vojvodich Radakovich) is calibrated for cycle-management governance through the AI infrastructure transition.
